observed: autocode_check_replay.replay writes its receipt (replay.json) and per-check logs (check-NN/) under run_dir/check-replay/<stem of the Validator output>. The stem (validator-01, validator-report-repair-01, ...) has no iteration in it, and the attempt number restarts at 1 in every iteration. So iteration 2's first Validator replay overwrites iteration 1's receipt in place. The rejection message saved in state still cites .../check-replay/validator-01/replay.json, but that file now holds another attempt's verdict. Leftover check-NN/ directories from the earlier, longer replay mix with the new logs. Archiving a rejected stage copies only iterations/ files, not the replay directory.
reproduction: In the investigation workspace I wrote .autocode/scratch/repro_341.py. It calls the real autocode_check_replay.replay with a fake scratch_run that writes a scratch-command.log per check directory. Step 1: a replay for output iterations/001/validator-01.json (source_revision rev1) with checks a (exit 0) and b (exit 1). It raises ValueError citing 'Receipt: .autocode/scratch/run/check-replay/validator-01/replay.json', and that file holds rev1. Step 2: a replay for iterations/002/validator-01.json (rev2) with one passing check c. Afterwards the receipt cited in step 1 holds verdict PASS, source_revision rev2. The directory holds check-01 (log 'c', from iteration 2) and check-02 (log 'b', left over from iteration 1). Receipt: .autocode/evidence/issue341-repro.json (exit 0). A single-command probe asserting the overwrite exits 0 on current code: .autocode/evidence/issue341-probe.json. Existing tests in tests.test_check_replay pass: 13 tests OK, .autocode/evidence/issue341-existing-tests.json.
root_cause: replay() at tools/autocode_check_replay.py:69 computes its output directory as Path(run_dir) / 'check-replay' / Path(record['output']).stem. It drops the parent directory iterations/<NNN>/ that makes the stage output unique. autocode_artifacts.stage_base numbers attempts per iteration (iterations/<NNN>/<slug>-<attempt>), so the same stem recurs in every iteration. Within one iteration it can also recur: reject_completed_stage archives a rejected output and unlinks the originals, so the attempt name can be reserved again. replay() then writes into the existing directory without checking it. It uses out.mkdir(exist_ok=True), overwrites replay.json, has scratch_run overwrite check-NN/, and never clears check directories beyond the new count. The failure message embeds that non-unique path, so the receipt it cites is rewritten by the next replay that shares the stem. archive_rejected_stage (tools/autocode_run_records.py:321) only copies iterations/<base>.* files, so nothing else keeps the replay output.
invariant: A check replay never writes into a directory an earlier replay wrote. Each replay's directory is unique to its own call (it includes the iteration and the attempt stem, and is never reused). The replay.json path quoted in a rejection message keeps holding that replay's verdict, source_revision and checks after any number of later replays in the same run.

conclusion: Reproduced: the check-replay directory is keyed only by the output file's stem (validator-01), which repeats in every iteration. A later replay therefore overwrites an earlier failed replay's receipt and logs, and the 'Receipt:' path saved in state ends up pointing at the wrong verdict. Fix it in tools/autocode_check_replay.py. Build the directory from the iteration directory plus the stem, and never reuse an existing directory: add a unique suffix when it exists. A receipt path, once cited, then stays valid and nothing needs to be copied at archive time.
fix_plan: In tools/autocode_check_replay.replay, derive the output directory from both the output's parent directory name (the iteration, e.g. '001') and its stem (e.g. 'validator-01'), e.g. run_dir/check-replay/001/validator-01.

If that directory already exists (a re-reserved attempt name after archive-and-unlink), pick a fresh unused sibling with a numeric or uuid suffix, created atomically with mkdir(exist_ok=False). No replay may write into a directory a previous replay used. Compute it before protected_oracles.replay so protected-test receipts also go to the unique directory.
